NEW-AP-U2-505.q: In a code language, each letter is shifted two places forward in the English alphabet (A → C, B → D). How is TEACHER written in that language?
NEW-AP-U2-505.e: T→V, E→G, A→C, C→E, H→J, E→G, R→T ⇒ VGCEJGT. (UFBDIFS shifts only one place.)

NEW-AP-U2-506.q: In a code, CAT is written as DBU. How is PEN written?
NEW-AP-U2-506.e: Each letter is replaced by the next letter (+1): C→D, A→B, T→U. So P→Q, E→F, N→O ⇒ QFO.

NEW-AP-U2-507.q: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:30?
NEW-AP-U2-507.e: Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30 × 3 − 5.5 × 30| = |90 − 165| = 75°. (When the minute hand is at 6, the hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4.)

NEW-AP-U2-508.q: Pointing to a photograph, Ramu says, 'This is the son of the only son of my grandfather.' If Ramu has no brother, who is in the photograph?
NEW-AP-U2-508.e: The only son of Ramu's grandfather = Ramu's father. The father's son — since Ramu has no brother — is Ramu himself. So the person in the photograph is Ramu.

NEW-AP-U2-509.q: A is B's brother. B is C's father. How is A related to C?
NEW-AP-U2-509.e: B is C's father; A is B's brother ⇒ A is C's father's brother, i.e. C's paternal uncle.

NEW-AP-U2-510.e: 2, 3, 5 and 11 are prime numbers; 9 (= 3 × 3) is composite — so it is the odd one out.

NEW-AP-U2-511.e: 16 (4²), 25 (5²), 36 (6²) and 64 (8²) are perfect squares; 48 is not a perfect square.

NEW-AP-U2-512.q: A man walks 10 m north, turns right and walks 5 m, then turns right again and walks 10 m. How far, and in which direction, is he from his starting point?
NEW-AP-U2-512.e: North 10 m → turning right means east, 5 m → turning right again means south, 10 m. The north and south movements cancel, so he is 5 m east of the starting point.

NEW-AP-U2-513.q: In the English alphabet, which letter is 4th to the right of the 10th letter from the left?
NEW-AP-U2-513.e: The 10th letter from the left is J. The 4th to its right = 10 + 4 = 14th letter, N.

NEW-AP-U2-514.q: Five students by height: Arun is taller than Balu; Balu is taller than Chandru; Dinesh is taller than Arun; Eswar is shorter than Chandru. Who is the tallest?
NEW-AP-U2-514.e: From the data: Dinesh > Arun > Balu > Chandru > Eswar. So Dinesh is the tallest and Eswar the shortest.

NEW-AP-U2-515.q:
Statements: All cats are animals. Some animals are dogs.
Conclusions: (I) All cats are dogs. (II) Some animals are cats.
NEW-AP-U2-515.e: Since all cats are animals, 'Some animals are cats' (II) definitely follows. No link is given between cats and dogs, so 'All cats are dogs' (I) cannot be concluded.

NEW-GS-U1-901.q: The SI unit of force is
NEW-GS-U1-901.e: The SI unit of force is the newton (N): the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s². Joule – work/energy; watt – power; pascal – pressure.

NEW-GS-U1-902.q: The SI unit of electrical resistance is
NEW-GS-U1-902.e: The SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω). Ampere – current; volt – potential difference; coulomb – charge (textbook).

NEW-GS-U1-903.q: One horse power (1 HP) is equal to
NEW-GS-U1-903.e: Horse power is a unit of power in the foot-pound-second system; 1 HP = 746 watts (textbook).

NEW-GS-U1-904.e: 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ J. This is the 'one unit' of electrical energy on an electricity bill (textbook).

NEW-GS-U1-905.q: The SI unit of the power of a lens is
NEW-GS-U1-905.e: Power of a lens = 1/focal length (in metres); its unit is the dioptre (D). Lux – illuminance; candela – luminous intensity.

NEW-GS-U1-906.q: In which medium is the speed of sound highest?
NEW-GS-U1-906.e: Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases. Sound needs a medium, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

NEW-GS-U1-907.q: The value of Avogadro's number is
NEW-GS-U1-907.e: The number of particles in one mole of a substance is Avogadro's number = 6.023 × 10²³ (textbook). 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C – charge of an electron; 9.8 m/s² – acceleration due to gravity.

NEW-GS-U1-908.q: Below what pH of the mouth does tooth enamel start to decay?
NEW-GS-U1-908.e: Tooth enamel (calcium phosphate), the hardest substance in the body, starts to decay when the pH in the mouth falls below 5.5; that is why toothpastes are basic (textbook).

NEW-GS-U1-909.q: The chemical name of baking soda is
NEW-GS-U1-909.e: Baking soda = sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃). Washing soda = sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O); limestone = calcium carbonate; common salt = sodium chloride.

NEW-GS-U1-910.q: The chemical name of Plaster of Paris is
NEW-GS-U1-910.e: Plaster of Paris = calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O); used for setting fractured bones and making statues. Gypsum = CaSO₄·2H₂O; quicklime = CaO; slaked lime = Ca(OH)₂.

NEW-GS-U1-911.q: The pH value of a neutral solution is
NEW-GS-U1-911.e: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14; pH 7 is neutral (pure water); below 7 is acidic; above 7 is basic.

NEW-GS-U1-912.q: The disease caused by deficiency of vitamin C is
NEW-GS-U1-912.e: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency – scurvy (bleeding gums). Vitamin A – night blindness; D – rickets; B1 (thiamine) – beriberi.

NEW-GS-U1-913.q: The hormone that lowers blood sugar level is
NEW-GS-U1-913.e: Insulin, secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, lowers blood sugar; glucagon, secreted by the alpha cells, raises it. Insulin deficiency – diabetes.

NEW-GS-U1-914.q: The pigment in red blood cells that carries oxygen is
NEW-GS-U1-914.e: Iron-containing haemoglobin combines with oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin and carries oxygen throughout the body. Chlorophyll – green plant pigment; melanin – skin pigment; keratin – protein of hair and nails.

NEW-GS-U1-915.q: The gas released by plants during photosynthesis is
NEW-GS-U1-915.e: In photosynthesis, plants convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose using sunlight and chlorophyll, and release oxygen: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

NEW-GS-U1-916.q: The largest gland in the human body is
NEW-GS-U1-916.e: The liver is the largest gland in the human body; it secretes bile. The pituitary is called the 'master gland'; the pancreas is a dual gland (exocrine + endocrine).

NEW-GS-U3-1001.q: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
NEW-GS-U3-1001.e: Through the efforts of A.O. Hume, the Indian National Congress was founded in Bombay on 28 December 1885; its first president was W.C. Bonnerjee.

NEW-GS-U3-1002.q: The Viceroy who partitioned Bengal (1905) was
NEW-GS-U3-1002.e: In the name of administrative convenience, but intending to divide the national movement, Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905; the Swadeshi movement arose against it; the partition was annulled in 1911.

NEW-GS-U3-1003.q: On which date did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
NEW-GS-U3-1003.e: On 13 April 1919 General Dyer opened fire on people gathered at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, against the Rowlatt Act. 5.2.1922 – Chauri Chaura; 12.3.1930 – start of the Dandi March; 8.8.1942 – Quit India resolution.

NEW-GS-U3-1004.q: Which event made Gandhiji withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement?
NEW-GS-U3-1004.e: In February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh, protesters set fire to a police station and killed 22 policemen; Gandhiji, who rejected violence, withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement.

NEW-GS-U3-1005.q: In which year did Gandhiji's Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) begin?
NEW-GS-U3-1005.e: On 12 March 1930 Gandhiji set out from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 volunteers, covered 241 miles in 24 days to reach Dandi, and broke the salt law on 6 April (textbook).

NEW-GS-U3-1006.q: The slogan 'Do or Die' is associated with which movement?
NEW-GS-U3-1006.e: When the Quit India resolution was passed in Bombay on 8 August 1942, Gandhiji gave the call 'Do or Die'.

NEW-GS-U3-1007.q:
Match:
(a) Lucknow Pact – 1. 1932
(b) Poona Pact – 2. 1916
(c) Cripps Mission – 3. 1946
(d) Cabinet Mission – 4. 1942
NEW-GS-U3-1007.e: Lucknow Pact (Congress–Muslim League) – 1916 (2); Poona Pact (Gandhi–Ambedkar) – 1932 (1); Cripps Mission – 1942 (4); Cabinet Mission – 1946 (3). Hence 2, 1, 4, 3.

NEW-GS-U3-1008.q: The year and place in which the Muslim League was founded
NEW-GS-U3-1008.e: The All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December 1906 (Aga Khan, Nawab Salimullah and others). The Pakistan Resolution was passed at the 1940 Lahore session.

NEW-GS-U3-1009.q: In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
NEW-GS-U3-1009.e: In the Battle of Plassey (1757), the English East India Company under Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal; it laid the foundation of British rule in India. 1764 – Battle of Buxar; 1799 – Fourth Mysore War.

NEW-GS-U3-1010.q: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' is associated with
NEW-GS-U3-1010.e: Lord Dalhousie applied the Doctrine of Lapse (1848), under which a state whose ruler died without a natural male heir was annexed to British rule (Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur). Subsidiary Alliance – Wellesley; Permanent Settlement – Cornwallis.

NEW-GS-U3-1011.e: Under the Subsidiary Alliance introduced by Lord Wellesley (1798), Indian rulers had to keep a British force in their territory and bear its cost; the Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to accept.

NEW-GS-U3-1012.e: Kautilya (Chanakya), minister of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the Arthashastra on politics and administration. Megasthenes – Indica; Bana – Harshacharita; Kalidasa – Shakuntalam.

NEW-GS-U3-1013.q: Which Mauryan emperor embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga war?
NEW-GS-U3-1013.e: Moved by the destruction of the Kalinga war (261 BCE), Ashoka gave up war, embraced Buddhism and spread the policy of 'Dhamma'.

NEW-GS-U3-1014.q: The Chinese pilgrim who visited India during the Gupta period was
NEW-GS-U3-1014.e: Fa-Hien (399–414 CE) came to India during the reign of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya). Hiuen Tsang came in Harsha's time; Marco Polo was a Venetian traveller.

NEW-GS-U3-1015.q: The Chinese pilgrim who came to India during Harsha's reign and studied at Nalanda University was
NEW-GS-U3-1015.e: Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) came to India in Harsha's time and studied at Nalanda; he wrote his travel account 'Si-Yu-Ki'. Ibn Battuta – time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Al-Biruni – time of Mahmud of Ghazni.

NEW-GS-U3-1016.q: The Sultan who shifted his capital from Delhi to Devagiri (Daulatabad) was
NEW-GS-U3-1016.e: In 1327 Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted the capital from Delhi to Devagiri and renamed it 'Daulatabad'; later he moved it back to Delhi. He also introduced token (copper) currency.

NEW-GS-U3-1017.q: The Mughal emperor who founded the new religious path 'Din-i-Ilahi' was
NEW-GS-U3-1017.e: Combining the good ideas of all religions, Akbar founded 'Din-i-Ilahi' in 1582; only a few, including Birbal, followed it.

NEW-GS-U3-1018.q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between
NEW-GS-U3-1018.e: In the First Battle of Panipat (1526) Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi and founded the Mughal Empire. Akbar–Hemu: Second Panipat (1556); Abdali–Marathas: Third Panipat (1761); Babur–Rana Sanga: Battle of Khanwa (1527).

NEW-GS-U3-1019.q: Who is called the 'Iron Man of India'?
NEW-GS-U3-1019.e: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, India's first Home Minister, who integrated over 500 princely states into the Indian Union, is the 'Iron Man of India'. Lajpat Rai – 'Lion of Punjab'; Tilak – 'Lokmanya'.

NEW-GS-U3-1020.q: Who declared, 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'?
NEW-GS-U3-1020.e: The Extremist leader Bal Gangadhar Tilak made this declaration; he ran the papers 'Kesari' (Marathi) and 'Maratha' (English).

NEW-GS-U3-1021.q: Who led the Indian National Army (INA) and gave the call 'Delhi Chalo'?
NEW-GS-U3-1021.e: In 1943 Subhas Chandra Bose took charge of the Indian National Army started by Rash Behari Bose and gave the calls 'Delhi Chalo' and 'Jai Hind'.

NEW-GS-U3-1022.q: India's national song 'Vande Mataram' appears in which book?
o: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
NEW-GS-U3-1022.e: 'Vande Mataram' appears in Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel 'Anandamath'. The national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' – Rabindranath Tagore; My Experiments with Truth – Gandhiji; The Discovery of India – Nehru.

NEW-GS-U5-1101.q: In which city is the headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India?
NEW-GS-U5-1101.e: The Reserve Bank of India started in Kolkata in 1935 and has had its headquarters in Mumbai since 1937.

NEW-GS-U5-1102.q: In India, which authority issues all currency notes except the ₹1 note?
o: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
NEW-GS-U5-1102.e: The RBI issues notes of ₹2 and above; the ₹1 note and coins are issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India (the ₹1 note carries the Finance Secretary's signature).

NEW-GS-U5-1103.q: In which year were 14 major commercial banks nationalised in India?
NEW-GS-U5-1103.e: On 19 July 1969 the Indira Gandhi government nationalised 14 major commercial banks; 6 more were nationalised in 1980. 1949 – RBI nationalised; 1955 – Imperial Bank became State Bank of India.

NEW-GS-U5-1104.q: The apex bank for agriculture and rural development is
NEW-GS-U5-1104.e: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development), set up in 1982, is the apex body for agricultural and rural credit. SIDBI – small industries; EXIM – exports and imports.

NEW-GS-U5-1105.q: The year of launch and aim of the 'Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana'
o: 2014 – a bank account for all (financial inclusion)
NEW-GS-U5-1105.e: Jan Dhan Yojana, launched on 28 August 2014, is a financial-inclusion scheme giving every household a zero-balance bank account, a RuPay card and insurance. 2019 – PM-KISAN (₹6,000 a year to farmers).

NEW-GS-U5-1106.q: The period of India's First Five-Year Plan was
NEW-GS-U5-1106.e: First Five-Year Plan: 1951–56 (Harrod–Domar model; priority to agriculture and irrigation). Second Plan 1956–61; Third Plan 1961–66.

NEW-GS-U5-1107.q: The period of India's last (Twelfth) Five-Year Plan was
NEW-GS-U5-1107.e: The Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–2017) was the last; its theme was 'faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth'. After it, NITI Aayog's vision documents replaced five-year plans.

NEW-GS-U5-1108.q: The Chairman of the Planning Commission was the
NEW-GS-U5-1108.e: The Prime Minister was the Chairman of the Planning Commission set up in 1950, and is also the Chairperson of NITI Aayog, which replaced it in 2015.

NEW-GS-U5-1109.q: The nature of the Indian economy is
NEW-GS-U5-1109.e: Since the public sector and the private sector work together in India, it is called a mixed economy.
